title: U.S. House · Connecticut's 2nd District
area: Eastern Connecticut, including Norwich, New London, Willimantic, and the state's rural northeastern and southeastern corners

context.text: Both the Democratic and Republican primaries for this seat were canceled after only one candidate qualified for each party's ballot line. The Cook Political Report rated this district D+4 based on 2024 presidential results.

summary.text: Joe Courtney is the Democratic incumbent for Connecticut's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2006. A lawyer and former public defender, he served in the Connecticut House of Representatives from 1987 to 1994 before entering Congress. He serves on the House Armed Services and Education and Workforce committees and is ranking member of the Armed Services Subcommittee on Seapower and Projection Forces.

background.text: Born in Hartford County, Connecticut, and graduated from Northwest Catholic High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Tufts University in 1975 and a law degree from the University of Connecticut School of Law in 1978.
Worked as a public defender before entering the legislature.
Represented Vernon in the Connecticut House of Representatives from 1987 to 1994, serving as House chairman of both the Public Health and Human Services committees.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2006 and has represented Connecticut's 2nd District since 2007, currently serving his tenth term.

Serves on the House Armed Services Committee and the Education and Workforce Committee; chaired the Armed Services Subcommittee on Seapower and Projection Forces from 2018 to 2022 and is now its ranking member. His official biography says he is the first known Connecticut member to lead a House naval oversight panel since 1873.

His official biography says he has worked for increased submarine production, which it credits with sustaining Electric Boat's workforce in southeastern Connecticut, and that he received the Navy's Distinguished Public Service Award from Navy Secretary Ray Mabus.

Founding co-chairman of the Congressional Dairy Farmers Caucus, and his official biography says he introduced the law designating the Eightmile River as part of the National Wild and Scenic Rivers System.
According to his official biography, lives in Vernon with his wife, Audrey, and their two children.

positions.summary: Co-sponsors a plan to let Americans age 50-64 buy into Medicare, alongside a reinsurance program and cost-sharing reductions to stabilize the individual insurance market.
positions.quote: The Courtney-Larson-Higgins plan would allow Americans age 50-64 to buy-in to Medicare, the system with the highest satisfaction rate of any health insurance program, according to a 2016 Gallup poll.

positions.summary: Supported the Revolution Wind offshore wind project supplying power to Connecticut and Rhode Island, and opposed the Trump administration's attempts to halt it.
positions.quote: At a time when Americans are being hit with increasing energy costs, flipping the on switch to start Revolution Wind will bring cheaper electricity to Connecticut's consumers

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Armed Services (Seapower and Projection Forces; Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees) in the 2025–2026 Congress.
Serves on the House Committee on Education and the Workforce in the 2025–2026 Congress.

Chaired the Armed Services Subcommittee on Seapower and Projection Forces in the 2021–2022 Congress, a panel with jurisdiction over Navy shipbuilding programs including the Groton-based submarine industrial base.

Introduced the CLINIC Assistance Act, which would create a Department of Labor grant program for law schools to set up consumer advocate programs helping patients appeal denied health insurance claims.
Co-led (with Rep. Nick LaLota) the Long Island Sound Stewardship and Restoration Reauthorization Act, which the House passed to reauthorize the EPA's Long Island Sound Grant Program.

candidates.name: George Austin
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced after the Republican primary was canceled

summary.text: George Austin is the Republican nominee for Connecticut's 2nd Congressional District; he is also on the ballot as the Independent Party of Connecticut nominee. A first-generation American, he describes himself as a tradesman and homebuilder for the past twenty years and is a first-time candidate. He says he is running on affordability, tax relief and housing costs.

background.text: Describes himself as a first-generation American.
Graduated from South Windsor High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Central Connecticut State University in 2014.
Has worked as a contractor; describes himself as a tradesman and homebuilder for the past twenty years.
Describes himself as a first-time candidate who accepted both the Republican and Independent Party of Connecticut nominations for Congress in 2026; the August 11 Republican primary was canceled.
Describes himself as a husband and father of two young men.
